bug_semantics: An administrator-controlled RSE creation request can persist HTML/JavaScript in the city, country_name, or ISP metadata fields. The WebUI then treats those stored strings as markup in two victim-facing paths: lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rses.js passes the raw API objects directly to DataTables columns, and lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js concatenates metadata values into HTML passed to jQuery.append. Loading the RSE Management list or an RSE detail page therefore executes the stored payload in the viewer's WebUI origin, where it can read JavaScript-accessible session/token material and act with the victim's authority.
flaw_origin: Commit 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 introduced the RSE-management WebUI feature as one ordinary commit. It added the create form and POST client for raw city/country_name/ISP values, the /rse, /rses, and /rses/add UI routes, the listing DataTable whose data source is the unencoded server response, and the detail-table helper that interpolates returned values into HTML. The persistence API predated or existed independently of the browser view, but this commit first created the executable rendering sinks and the documented WebUI create/trigger lifecycle.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names Hannes Hansen <hannes.jakob.hansen@cern.ch> as both author and committer, contains the single message 'WebUI: added support for getting informations, creation and deletion of RSEs and attributes Fix #80', and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-h9fp-p2p9-873q documents POST /proxy/rses/XSSTEST with script payloads in city/country_name/ISP, execution on both the RSE list and detail views, affected rucio-webui ranges <35.8.3, >=36.0.0rc1,<38.5.4, and >=39.0.0rc1,<39.3.1, and patched releases 35.8.3/38.5.4/39.3.1. In 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735, add_rse.js lines 13-40 reads those fields and sends them unchanged; rses.js lines 20-33 initializes DataTables with data:data and raw city/country_name/ISP columns; rse.js lines 13-25 inserts data[sorted_keys[i]] into a constructed HTML row. `git log -L 20,33:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rses.js a3618f46...^` reaches 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 as the sole origin of the listing sink. `git log -L 13,29:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js 24468abb...^` reaches the same BIC through later non-causal edits. Path-scoped `git log --all -S'data: data'` and `-S"data[sorted_keys[i]] + ''"` each identify 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 as the addition and the 2026 security commits as removals. `git ls-tree -r c77904c15e1958ad9f32e862b9e9714e48076434 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rses.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/rses.html` returns no entries; a parent-tree grep has generic list_rses callers but no city/country_name/ISP metadata table, directly proving the vulnerable UI mechanism absent in the immediate parent. The BIC creates both files rather than moving them, has one parent, and `git cat-file -p` shows no attribution trailers, so no squash decomposition is needed. Tag containment places the BIC in 1.18.0 and in vulnerable boundary tags 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0. The 35.8.2..35.8.3 path diff contains direct listing fix a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003, which copies each field through jQuery .text() before DataTables, plus detail fix 24468abb0e076fa83d5f3bc6db6050182fed4c79, which constructs cells and assigns metadata with .text(). Equivalent listing/detail backports are abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7/e8848dfc66f79e5cc9d1077ef371d971dd290db1 in 38.5.4 and 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41/1559c59e1fc571f75775fb4f656d752b32309e24 in 39.3.1. Thus each immediately prior tag contains the BIC and each advisory-patched boundary contains both sink corrections.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by output handling, not merely by accepting flexible metadata: stored strings become executable only when the RSE-management client inserts them as HTML. History tracing converges on 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 because that smallest non-merge commit created both unsafe views and the matching create UI; later edits retained the same interpolation, and the immediate parent lacks the pages/files and metadata rendering mechanism. The 2026 remediation is split by sink family: the detail-view jQuery concatenation is removed first and the listing DataTable exposure is closed by a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 on the 35-LTS line, with equivalent commits present at the other two patched boundaries. Because the listing is the advisory's demonstrated trigger and remained exploitable until a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003, that direct commit is the lifecycle closure recorded as fix_sha/direct_fix_sha; the companion detail fixes are retained in evidence. Finally, the BIC's raw commit object contains only a named human author/committer and no AI marker. Under BIC-only attribution, the causal introducer is therefore NOT_AI regardless of any evidence on later remediation commits.
